snippet.title: Iconic 5-Storey Michael Jackson Mural at 11th Street & 1st Avenue – A Vibrant Tribute in NYC

snippet.title: Prince Jackson Shares the Most Meaningful Items He Still Has from His Dad Michael Jackson ❤️
snippet.description:
Prince Jackson, son of the legendary Michael Jackson, opens up about the most meaningful items he still cherishes from his father.

In this heartfelt conversation, he talks about his dad’s model train station at Neverland Ranch, where they spent quality time together designing scenery and watching the trains run. He still keeps one of the train cars as a treasured memory.

He also shares the story of a special notebook from his film school days at home. Michael Jackson had invited a professor from UCLA or USC to teach him and his cousins filmmaking. The notebook contains film shots, framing notes, and most importantly — Michael Jackson’s own handwritten notes in red ink. Prince’s cousin Taj preserved it and later gifted it to him.

These two items hold immense emotional value for Prince as they represent the precious father-son moments he shared with the King of Pop.

🎙️ From Prince Jackson’s recent interview

What makes this footage even more historically significant is that the second show took place on September 10, 2001 — just one day before the world changed forever. This concert unknowingly marked the end of an era in entertainment history.

Michael Jackson remains the best-selling solo music artist of all time with over 350 million records sold worldwide. His influence on music, dance, and performance continues to inspire generations across the globe.

snippet.title: Neverland Ranch of Michael Jackson | Michael Jackson’s Private Paradise |iconic estate #mj
snippet.description:
Neverland Ranch was created by Michael Jackson in 1988. He bought this 2,700-acre property in California and named it Neverland after the magical place from Peter Pan. His dream was to build a place where children could be happy and he could live like a child forever. That’s why he made an amusement park, zoo, train, lake with fountains, gardens and his beautiful mansion.

In the beginning, many children visited Neverland and it became a symbol of joy and magic. But after the serious allegations against Michael Jackson in 1993 and 2003, the situation changed completely. Public visits stopped, security was increased, and Neverland was no longer open for children. Due to these controversies and financial problems, Michael Jackson had to sell the property in 2008.

Today, Neverland Ranch is located in Los Olivos, Santa Barbara County, California. It was bought by a businessman in 2020 and is now a private residence. The public is not allowed to visit. However, the lake with twin fountains, the grand gate, gardens, mansion, swimming pool and the famous Neverland sign are still standing — exactly as you can see in this video.

A place that was once full of dreams and laughter now stands quiet and private.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Last Photo Before Death 2009 💔 | Sold for $500,000 #michaeljackson
snippet.description:
A photograph the world was never meant to see… 💔

On June 25, 2009, Michael Jackson was rushed from his home to UCLA Medical Center in an ambulance. Outside, a huge crowd of media and photographers waited.

As the ambulance moved, photographer Chris Weiss captured the final known photo of Michael through the window — showing him lying on a stretcher with an oxygen mask on his face.

This haunting image was later sold to OK! Magazine for approximately $500,000. It reportedly changed the paparazzo’s life forever.

Even in his last moments, when he needed peace the most, privacy was taken away from one of the greatest artists the world has ever known.

Some losses never stop hurting… and this was one of them.

snippet.title: Inside Michael Jackson’s Hayvenhurst Estate | Rare Tour of Thriller Jackets, Awards & Studio #mj
snippet.description:
Rare Glimpse Inside Hayvenhurst Estate – Michael Jackson’s Family Home in Encino, California

Hayvenhurst Estate is the famous family mansion where Michael Jackson lived for many years before moving to Neverland Ranch. The property, located at 4641 Hayvenhurst Avenue in Encino, has been carefully preserved by the Jackson family.

This private tour shows several iconic areas and items:

1. Michael’s Private Recording Studio – The place where he worked on parts of his biggest albums like Thriller and Bad.

2. Trophy Room – Filled with his award collection including multiple Grammy Awards (he won a record 8 Grammys in one night), American Music Awards, MTV Video Music Awards, and many international honors.

4. Iconic Memorabilia – Michael’s signature black fedora, the famous crystal-encrusted white glove, and other performance items.

5. Thriller 100 Million Plaque – A special commemorative award celebrating Thriller becoming the best-selling album of all time with over 100 million copies sold worldwide.

6. Original Thriller Costumes – The red and yellow Varsity Jacket (Letterman jacket) from the early scenes and the distressed Red Zombie Jacket from the graveyard dance sequence in the Thriller music video.

5. Jackson 5 Family Photos – Early images showcasing the brothers’ journey from their beginnings.

These items represent some of the most important pieces in music history and offer fans a look at Michael Jackson’s creative world and achievements.

Rare Glimpse Inside Hayvenhurst Estate – Michael Jackson’s Family Home in Encino, California

Hayvenhurst Estate is the famous family mansion where Michael Jackson lived for many years before moving to Neverland Ranch. The property, located at 4641 Hayvenhurst Avenue in Encino, has been carefully preserved by the Jackson family.

This private tour shows several iconic areas and items:

1. Michael’s Private Recording Studio – The place where he worked on parts of his biggest albums like Thriller and Bad.

2. Trophy Room – Filled with his award collection including multiple Grammy Awards (he won a record 8 Grammys in one night), American Music Awards, MTV Video Music Awards, and many international honors.

4. Iconic Memorabilia – Michael’s signature black fedora, the famous crystal-encrusted white glove, and other performance items.

5. Thriller 100 Million Plaque – A special commemorative award celebrating Thriller becoming the best-selling album of all time with over 100 million copies sold worldwide.

6. Original Thriller Costumes – The red and yellow Varsity Jacket (Letterman jacket) from the early scenes and the distressed Red Zombie Jacket from the graveyard dance sequence in the Thriller music video.

5. Jackson 5 Family Photos – Early images showcasing the brothers’ journey from their beginnings.

These items represent some of the most important pieces in music history and offer fans a look at Michael Jackson’s creative world and achievements.
